newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares slip to lower close as Dow slides.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares slip to lower close as Dow slides.

text.p: Milan shares slipped to a sharply lower close on Friday as an easier opening on Wall Street and the lower tone to most European bourses put buyers on the defensive and kept international investors out of the market.

After a delayed start to trading due to technical problems stock moved lower after Thursday's overnight fall in U.S. stock and then sank further when Wall Street opened this afternoon. Warburg confirmed its downgrade on ENI putting the oil company's shares on the defensive losing some 2.5 percent.
The all-share Mibtel index closed off 1.87 percent at 12,417 and the Mib30 index down 2.11 percent at 18,564.

ENI shares slipped as investment bank SBC Warburg confirmed that it had downgraded its recommendation for Italy's oil and chemical giant ENI to a "hold" from a "buy" and had also trimmed its earnings forecast for 1996.

SBC Warburg oil analyst Gavin White in London said he had trimmed his 1996 net profit forecast by three percent down to 4.5 trillion lire due to difficult conditions during the second half of the year in the chemicals sector.
But White upgraded his 1997 earnings forecast by four percent to 5.0 trillion lire net profit on currency factors.
Dealers said that early losses were pared back by mid-morning on government optimism over a agreement in the long-running metalworkers dispute.

Italy's Labour minister Tiziano Treu said the chances of an agreement had improved after the government met unions this morning. The government has called a meeting on Monday between unions leaders and Italy's employers' federation.

Other blue chips eased with Fiat off 1.41 percent at 5,375 lire, Olivetti slipped 2.35 percent to 718.6 lire, Montedison was off 2.0 percent to 1,320 lire. One share to stand out was Pirelli which continued its good run up 0.72 percent at 3,504.
